source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Provide a detailed account of the inspection process, including the date & time of the inspection, the name(s) of the inspecting officer(s), and the location of the building.

3. Record specific fire-safety checks conducted.
Clearly document each individual fire-safety check performed during the inspection (e.g., fire alarms, emergency lighting, sprinkler systems, fire extinguishers, exit signs, and door operations). Include descriptions of each check and the result (whether it passed or failed).

4. Document problems identified.
For each failed check, clearly describe the nature and location of the problem in detail. Include photographs or drawings when possible to give a visual account of the issue.

5. Specify regulatory benchmarks.
Cite the specific fire safety standards or regulations that each failed check contravenes (local, state, or national).

6. Point out immediate dangers.
Identify any immediate and serious hazards that need urgent attention (e.g., blocked fire exits
